Connecting Plato

Connecting your Plato account

At the end of this guide, your AI shows real free times from Plato and books patients in the way you choose.

Only a Plato admin can make an API key. If you are not the Plato admin, do Step 1 together with them.

Before you start

You need:

  • A Plato login with the admin role.
  • Your 41 Sales Team dashboard, with the owner or admin role.
  • Your opening hours, lunch break and the dates you are closed.
  • About 15 minutes.
  • A phone that is not set up as an admin number on your dashboard, for the test in Step 12.

What we ask you for

FieldRequired?Where to find it
Clinic account in PlatoYesPlato's name for your clinic. It is the word after /api/ in your Plato address. Plato support can confirm it.
API keyYesIn Plato: System Setup → General Settings → API, then Generate API Key. Treat it like a password.

What happens in this guide

Connecting Plato has six stages. Step 1 is in Plato. Steps 2 to 11 are on one screen in your dashboard, in four parts: Test the key, Name calendars, Opening hours and Who books.

The six stages of connecting Plato, from making the key to pressing Connect Plato.

Two buttons matter. Test the connection reads from Plato and saves nothing. Connect Plato saves the key and every choice together, or nothing at all.

What Test the connection and Connect Plato each read and save.

Step by step

01

Make an API key in Plato

  1. In Plato, open System Setup → General Settings.
  2. Open the API tab.
  3. Press Generate API Key.
  4. Copy the key.

Send the key to nobody. Paste it into your dashboard only.

Screenshot to come: the Plato screen System Setup → General Settings → API, with the Generate API Key button.

02

Open Plato on the Connections screen

  1. In your dashboard, go to Settings → Connections.
  2. Press the Booking chip to show booking systems only.
  3. Under Add more, find Plato. It reads Free to connect.
  4. Press Connect.

Settings, Connections before Plato is connected: Nothing connected yet, and the Plato card under Add more.

03

Enter your clinic account and key

The Connect Plato screen opens on part 1 of 4, Test the key.

  1. Type your clinic account in Clinic account in Plato.
  2. Paste the key into API key. It shows as dots.
  3. Press Test the connection.

The test saves nothing. Nothing is stored until you press Connect Plato in Step 11.

Part 1, Test the key: the clinic account, the key as dots, and the Test the connection button.

04

Check the free times are yours

A green box reads Plato answered, with the number of calendars it found and up to three free times.

  1. Open your Plato diary for the day shown.
  2. Check that each time is free in Plato.
  3. Press Name the calendars.

After the test: three calendars found, three free times to check against your diary. Nothing is saved yet.

When your diary has no free time in the next days, the box says so. The key still works. Press Name the calendars.

The key works, but Plato shows no free time in the next days.

A red line under API key means the test failed. Find the line under If something goes wrong, fix it, and press Test the connection again.

05

Name the calendars your patients know

Part 2 of 4, Name calendars, lists every calendar in Plato. Each box starts with the name from Plato.

  1. Change a name to the one your patients use, such as the therapist or the room. A name stops at 60 characters.
  2. Switch off any calendar your AI must never book, such as admin blocks.
  3. Check the badge. It counts the calendars your AI may book.
  4. Press Next: set opening hours.

Part 2, Name calendars: each box starts with the Plato name, with a switch for each calendar.

A name stops at 60 characters. One calendar switched off: the badge reads 2 of 3 bookable.

Next stays off until at least one calendar is switched on.

06

Check your opening hours

Part 3 of 4, Opening hours, shows a week. It starts with Monday to Friday 09:00 to 18:00, Saturday 09:00 to 13:00 and Sunday closed, or with the hours you saved before.

  1. For each day, set the opening and the closing time.
  2. Switch off a day you are closed. It reads Closed.
  3. Under Each appointment, pick the length of one appointment. 30 minutes is the default.

Part 3, Opening hours as first shown: the default week, Last start empty, Lunch off, 30 minutes each.

07

Set a last start and a lunch break

Both are optional. Leave Last start empty, and an appointment only has to end by closing time.

  1. Type a Last start for a day. Your AI offers no time after it on that day.
  2. Switch on Lunch for a day and set its start and end. Your AI offers no time that overlaps it.

Monday to Friday with a last start of 17:00 and lunch 13:00 to 14:00. Saturday has neither.

A red line under the week names what to fix. Next: choose who books stays off until you fix it.

A closing time before the opening time: the red line says which day and what to set.

08

Set the booking limits

  1. Under Earliest new booking, pick how much notice a new booking needs. 1 hour is the default.
  2. Under Furthest booking, pick how far ahead your AI may book. 30 days is the default.
  3. Under Closed dates, pick a date and press Add date for each public holiday or day off. Up to 60 dates.
  4. Press Next: choose who books.

Booking limits: the notice, how far ahead, and the closed dates with the Add date button.

09

Choose who books

Part 4 of 4, Who books. Pick one:

Your AI books, your team confirmsThe time is held in Plato as not yet confirmed. The patient hears your team will confirm. Your team gets a WhatsApp alert. This is the default.
Your AI books itThe appointment goes into Plato as confirmed. The patient hears it is booked.
Your team books itYour AI shows real free times and takes the patient's choice. Your team books it in Plato.

Part 4, Who books: the three choices, the two hand-over rules, and the Connect Plato button.

10

Choose when a person steps in

Under Hand to a person when, switch on the rules you want. Your AI stops and alerts your team on WhatsApp, whatever you picked under Who books.

  • The patient is new: their WhatsApp number is not in Plato yet. Your team creates the record and books. Off by default.
  • A change or cancel comes in late: pick 12, 24 or 48 hours before the appointment. On by default, at 24 hours.

Both hand-over rules switched on, with the 24 hours choice.

11

Press Connect Plato

Press Connect Plato. One save stores the key and every choice from Steps 5 to 10 together.

A red banner above the buttons means nothing was saved. The form keeps your entries. Fix what the banner names, and press Connect Plato again.

A failed save: nothing was stored, and the form stays as it was.

When the save works, the Plato page opens with the green Working pill and Connected as followed by your clinic account.

The Plato page right after the save: Working, and Connected as your clinic account.

On Settings → Connections, the Plato card now sits under Connected.

Settings, Connections after connecting: the Plato card has moved up to Connected.

12

Test it from your own phone

  1. From your test phone, message your business WhatsApp number and ask for an appointment.
  2. Pick one of the times your AI offers.
  3. Give a full name when your AI asks for it.
  4. Check Plato: the appointment shows on the calendar you named.
  5. Check your WhatsApp: your team got the booking alert, if you chose a team step.

The full test, with a test patient, a move, a cancel and a hand-over, is in How your AI books with Plato at docs.41labs.ai/hermes/plato-how-booking-works.

Checklist

Good to know

  • Every setting is on the Plato page afterwards, under Settings → Connections → Plato. Who books, the hand-over rules and the calendar switches save at once. The hours and the limits have their own Save hours and Save limits buttons.
  • Your AI never asks a patient for an NRIC. A new patient is added with name and phone only.
  • A patient can see, move or cancel only appointments under their own WhatsApp number.
  • When Plato does not answer, your AI hands the booking to your team and never guesses a time.
  • To change the key, make a new one in Plato, press Connect again on the Plato page, and enter it.
  • Press Disconnect Plato at the bottom of the Plato page to stop. The dialog says what stops and what stays.
  • How bookings, moves, cancels and hand-overs work: How your AI books with Plato at docs.41labs.ai/hermes/plato-how-booking-works.

The Disconnect Plato? dialog: bookings stay in Plato, the key is deleted, you can connect again any time.
